Yes. **Zero-adjusted approaches have been applied to helminth infection data**, including schistosomiasis and fecal egg counts. In this literature, the relevant terms include **zero-inflated** and **hurdle** regression; these are related ways to model outcomes with many zero counts, but they are not identical models.

Examples found:

- A **2024 study of schoolchildren in southern Ghana** explicitly used zero-inflated and hurdle regression models to analyze schistosomiasis data. DOI: [10.1371/journal.pone.0304681](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0304681).
- A **2020 study of rural schoolchildren in southern Ethiopia** used zero-inflated regression to analyze helminth infections. DOI: [10.1371/journal.pntd.0008002](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pntd.0008002).
- A **2023 conference abstract** reported fitting a zero-inflated negative-binomial model to fecal egg counts, though the search result did not provide a DOI.

So this is not merely a theoretical possibility: there are published applications. The examples above establish use, but further review of each full paper would be needed to assess model fit, assumptions, and whether a zero-adjusted model was preferable to alternatives.

FINAL DECISION: YES
